stories.headline: Don't be surprised if Jordan Love makes history and Mendoza performs like a QB1
stories.summary: Elite WRs compensate for the lack of a run game in Green Bay, while there's unwarranted caution for Vegas' QB.
stories.body:
Each week in the NFL is its own story -- full of surprises, both positive and negative -- and fantasy football managers must decide what to believe and what not to believe moving forward. Perhaps we can help. If any of these thoughts come true ... don't be surprised!

NOTE: All mention of fantasy points is for PPR formats, unless otherwise mentioned.

Don't be surprised if ... Green Bay Packers QB Jordan Love becomes the 10th to pass for 5,000 yards in a season

MVP candidate Love continues to shine, throwing for 372 yards in Sunday's high-scoring road victory over the New England Patriots. With eight games left in the regular season, Love boasts a league-leading 2,618 passing yards, pacing toward 4,945 yards. Nine quarterbacks in NFL history have thrown for 5,000 yards, doing so 15 times. Matthew Stafford, Justin Herbert, Patrick Mahomes (twice) and -- of course -- Jameis Winston are the only active QBs to have done so.

The Packers cannot run the football effectively, forcing Love to throw more than the team's original plan. Love threw for 4,159 yards in his first season as starter back in 2023 but had 11 interceptions, and the team went 9-8. They wanted Love to take fewer chances, release the ball quicker and play more efficiently. Last season, the Packers went 9-5-1 in Love's 15 starts, as he threw for only 3,381 yards with a mere six interceptions. The Packers were fifth in the league in rushing in 2024 and 15th in 2025. That plan worked, and it figured to be the plan again.

Let's just say things haven't worked out in the running game -- thanks to offensive line and running back issues -- and there is little indication that will change in the coming weeks and months. The Packers are last in the NFL with 68.2 rushing yards per game. (For perspective, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers average 163.9.) The Packers average a brutal 3.0 yards per carry because healthy, proven options are limited. Love must throw often for the team to succeed and he has a pair of top-10 WRs in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. The Packers are 6-3, in last place in a tough division, but their path to January is Love piling on numbers.

Sticking with the powerful NFC North, it sure would be anything but bold to predict Minnesota Vikings WR Justin Jefferson will return to WR1 status now that the franchise reunited with a competent QB in Kirk Cousins. Watching Carson Wentz against the Buffalo Bills on Monday was painful, regardless of rooting interest and Jefferson looked miserable. Now he won't be! What if this division now boasts more than half of the top 10 WRs in fantasy this season? Assume the two Packers, plus Jefferson, Detroit Lions star Amon-Ra St. Brown and ... has anyone noticed Chicago Bears WR Luther Burden III is currently No. 10? Inconsistent but tantalizing Lion Jameson Williams is 19th in WR scoring, but capable of delivering 20-point outings at any time. How about six of the top 10 WRs in one division? Perhaps!

Don't be surprised if ... Las Vegas Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza performs like a deep-league QB1 option

I suppose one could reasonably debate whether the Raiders did the right thing in moving Cousins to the Vikings because it means the team must turn to Mendoza, the top pick in the NFL draft, potentially before he is ready. Then again, how do you find out if a QB is ready? Watch Mendoza step right in and perform much the way Cousins was doing, rocking the play-action pass and leaning heavily on TE Brock Bowers and RB Ashton Jeanty (as a receiver). Perhaps the Raiders will barely adjust a gameplan that is working. The Raiders are eighth in points this season. They don't think Mendoza will fail. Why should we?

Fantasy managers should be aggressive in adding Mendoza, though not necessarily activating him this week against a Seattle Seahawks defense that stymied Kansas City Chiefs QB Mahomes in Week 7. Then again, the Seahawks permitted 30 points in three games this season, to QBs Caleb Williams, Brock Purdy and ... Marcus Mariota! The Seahawks haven't seen Mendoza before. Again, I am not saying he scores 20 fantasy points or the Raiders score 20 points, but let's not be so dismissive. Perhaps the Raiders will even win the game at home.

After Seattle, the Raiders face the Denver Broncos, who rank 19th in permitting QB fantasy points this season. They're not No. 2, like the Seahawks. The Broncos get thrown on and they are permitting 355 yards per game, fourth in the NFL. It's a common mistake in evaluating fantasy options for managers to simply assume because everyone told them the Broncos were formidable. The Raiders also face the Los Angeles Chargers, Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans before the end of the season.

Only the Packers rank worse in rushing yards per game. The Raiders must throw the football, and Mendoza is certainly capable of making the same throws that Cousins was thriving at. Also, who are the QBs outside the top 10 in season scoring that may be starters for deep-league fantasy managers? Bryce Young, Tyler Shough, Stafford, Bo Nix? Why can't Mendoza be comparable for fantasy scoring? OK, don't expect Cousins-type numbers for the rookie, but I don't think we will be ranking Mendoza so cautiously after this week.

Another Raiders thought: Jeanty may not be the RB1 option so many fantasy managers expected, but he isn't a fantasy bust. He is 14th in running back scoring because he leads the position in receptions and he boasts more receiving yards than rushing ones. That is not entirely his fault as the Raiders struggle to run block. Jeanty is an electric option as a receiver, averaging 8.8 yards per catch, which is excellent for a running back. No top 30 RB had more receiving yards than they did rushing yards last season, though Kenny Gainwell came relatively close as a Pittsburgh Steeler. Jeanty may do so.

Don't be surprised if ... San Francisco 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey fails to rush for 1,000 yards

This isn't the first time we have discussed McCaffrey and his lack of volume this year, but really, this is all working out quite well for fantasy managers. Only three running backs boast more fantasy points than McCaffrey, even though he's tied for 22nd in rushing attempts (with Rhamondre Stevenson and Omarion Hampton). Oh, so you think McCaffrey must have a million receptions, right? Nope, his 36 catches are tied with Kyren Williams for third among RBs, but this is hardly a pace for 102 receptions, like last season. It is a pace for 76 catches.

Credit the 49ers for keeping the mercurial McCaffrey productive and healthy. Many were skeptical. He totaled a ridiculous 413 touches last season. Everyone expected some regression, but now he is pacing toward a manageable 292 touches. That is a huge dropoff and, while acknowledging McCaffrey has gone from averaging 24.5 fantasy points per game to 20.8 points is a big deal, we certainly cannot complain! McCaffrey has 10 touchdowns. He hasn't missed a game. He remains a fantasy star despite pacing for just 971 rushing yards.

Still, backup 49er Kaelon Black remains available in 65% of ESPN standard leagues. I think he should be more popular for the final months, not only if one rosters McCaffrey, but just in general. If McCaffrey were to get hurt (and nobody is rooting for this), this would be a potential RB1 option. Of course, we may say this about myriad RBs available in at least 50% of ESPN standard leagues, right? Or would we?

Kansas City Chiefs rookie Emmett Johnson looks like a future star and the Chiefs are trying harder to get the football to this fellow in open space, where he is dynamic. Nobody wants Kenneth Walker III to get injured either, but Johnson could be a legit RB1 if he gets a chance. The Chiefs and 49ers are built and managed well. Their backup RBs could be special. Would Seth McGowan rock if the Indianapolis Colts had traded the great Jonathan Taylor? Perhaps, but it is not the same as Black and Johnson. Khalil Herbert in Atlanta? C'mon. Justice Hill with the Ravens? Detroit's Sione Vaki? No, Black and Johnson stand out to me.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye USMNT's Balogun, Freeman for Pochettino
stories.summary: United States internationals Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman could be following Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
United States internationals Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman could be following coach Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, while Bayern Munich star Michael Olise is still being tailed by Real Madrid. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United have added United States duo Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman to their shortlist, TEAMtalk reports. Monaco striker Balogun, 25, and Villarreal defender Freeman, 22, are seen as two ideal candidates to land in January due to their familiarity with the USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino. Sources have told ESPN that Pochettino has agreed a deal to become the next manager at United and replace the fired Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. The Red Devils have been monitoring Freeman for some time, but could now step up their interest following his impressive performances under Pochettino for the USMNT. Balogun has said that he will look to seal a move away from Monaco in the next transfer window, having seen his proposed move to Everton fall through in the summer.

- Real Madrid remain interested in Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise, after previously being linked with him during the summer, according to L'Equipe. The 24-year-old is reported to have multiple top clubs in Europe 'dreaming' of signing him next summer, when he will enter the final two years of his contract at the Allianz Arena. Olise scored in France's 3-1 Nations League defeat against Italy on Thursday.

- Liverpool are keen on Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic, Florian Plettenberg reports. The Reds are monitoring the 19-year-old regularly after placing him on their shortlist of options for next summer, and he could be seen as a potential long term successor to Virgil van Dijk, who is yet to sign an extension on his current deal which is set to expire in June. There is no release clause in Vuskovic's contract, with his transfer expected to require a proposal worth in the region of €100 million.

- Chelsea right back Malo Gusto is attracting interest from Manchester City and Manchester United, according to talkSPORT. Both clubs are keeping tabs on the situation of the 23-year-old, who has only made three starts in the Premier League this season. The Blues would demand an offer worth £75 million before agreeing to part ways with him, in a deal that could see Gusto reunite with former manager Enzo Maresca at the Etihad Stadium.

- Juventus are interested in Tottenham Hotspur's Destiny Udogie and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde as new left backs,according to Corriere dello Sport. Udogie, 23, has made just two starts in the Premier League this season as the second choice option to Andy Robertson, and he has been identified as a player that the Bianconeri could acquire to reinforce the left side of their defense in January. Balde, 23, has also struggled to garner first team minutes and is linked with an exit from Camp Nou.

ESPN sources
- Manchester United are relaxed about the future of captain Bruno Fernandes despite the midfielder rejecting a second contract offer, sources have told ESPN. United and Fernandes' representatives are in talks about extending the 32-year-old's stay at Old Trafford. Fernandes has twice rejected improved terms, but United remain confident a deal will be agreed. Read

Other rumors
- AC Milan and Roma remain admirers of Real Madrid striker Endrick. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Barcelona won't listen to offers for midfielder Gavi despite his limited playing time this season. (Marca)

- Juventus winger Francisco Conceição is intending to stay put at the club despite links to the Premier League. (Fabrizio Romano)

- Atlético Madrid appreciate Arsenal midfielder Martín Zubimendi, but aren't currently pursuing a move for him amid reports of a potential swap deal involving Julián Álvarez. (Fabrizio Romano)

- Bournemouth have no plans to part ways with midfielder Alex Scott, winger Rayan or forward Junior Kroupi in the January transfer window. (Daily Telegraph)

- Juventus are looking at Crystal Palace defender Tyrick Mitchell. (Tuttosport)

- Liverpool, Manchester United and Newcastle United are monitoring Lazio defender Oliver Provstgaard. (Ekrem Konur)

- Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest are interested in Santos and Brazil international attacking midfielder Gabriel Bontempo. (TEAMtalk)

- Bayer Leverkusen striker Victor Boniface wants to leave the club in January. (Florian Plettenberg)

- Fulham are among several Premier League teams tracking Real Betis winger Rodrigo Riquelme. (TEAMtalk)

- Napoli are keen on Monza forward Gustavo Varela. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

stories.headline: Donovan Mitchell's renewed faith in Cleveland fuels the Cavs' future
stories.summary: Mitchell made two commitments this summer: his marriage and his extension with the Cavs. Now it's up to him to keep pushing Cleveland forward.
stories.body:
A FEW WEEKS before Donovan Mitchell and singer Coco Jones were set to be married, they had another reason to rejoice.

It was early July. The pair had gathered for a joint bachelor-bachelorette party before they were officially married in August at a private residence in upstate New York. Seven groomsmen and six bridesmaids joined the couple to commemorate their upcoming nuptials, but Jones and Mitchell took a moment for themselves during the trip. They knew their future was together, and now they were about to solidify where they'd be building it.

The Cleveland Cavaliers were poised to offer Mitchell a four-year, $273 million contract extension that would keep them in Cleveland through 2031. And he was set to sign it, even though he understood that by waiting until next summer, he could earn an additional $80 million.

For years, he had reiterated how much he loved the team and the city. He didn't want a lingering contract negotiation to loom over the 2026-27 Cavs season. He wanted to make the commitment.

"The summer of celebrations," Mitchell told ESPN.

It was a welcome reprieve. His summer was preceded by yet another spring of disappointment.

For the first time in his career, despite making the playoffs in each of his first nine seasons, Mitchell advanced to the conference finals. The Cavs had survived a seven-game first-round series against the Toronto Raptors and then won a Game 7 on the road against the top-seeded Detroit Pistons. Mitchell took it as a sign of growth, that they were finally ready for whatever adversity would arrive. It was Cleveland's deepest run without LeBron James in 34 years.

Then they ran out of gas.

An embarrassing sweep at the hands of the eventual champion New York Knicks finished their 2026 playoff run and left Cleveland with a losing postseason record overall (8-10).

A familiar feeling sat with the franchise.

"In the moment it kind of leaves a sour taste in your mouth," Mitchell told ESPN. "But as you sit ... you have to realize, OK, you've done something you haven't done before. OK. Now that's great, but I wouldn't call it an accomplishment. I would just call it a step."

In Mitchell's four years in Cleveland, the Cavs have consistently been one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference, racking up 51-, 48-, 64- and 52-win seasons.

A regular-season juggernaut. And then a playoff disappointment.

As the Cavaliers entered yet another offseason with the same core, the landscape of the Eastern Conference changed around them.

Rumors of a homecoming with James percolated across the organization and the league, but James chose Philadelphia. In turn, the Cavs bet on continuity, on changes along the margins.

Sources inside and out of the organization said the Cavs weren't interested in trading forward Evan Mobley, who's on a max rookie contract. After acquiring former MVP James Harden at last February's deadline, they re-signed the 37-year-old to a new three-year contract. And one day after the season ended, the team squashed any speculation about the status of coach Kenny Atkinson.

And then Mitchell cemented his commitment.

"When doubt lingers in an organization, it's not great," Atkinson said. "Everybody's just unsettled. So, the fact that Don locked it up, that was huge. It's like a sigh of relief. You know you're going to have your leader and it's going to give you stability. It helps you just move forward quicker."

Their biggest move was acquiring wing Peyton Watson to fill the role as a fifth starter to help protect Mitchell and Harden on defense. So far, their bet hasn't paid off. In fact, the Cavs' starting lineup has a minus-12.0 NET rating this season. Only the starters for Phoenix and Utah have been worse.

It echoes an underwhelming start of the Cavs season. They are 6-6 with skepticism around the league and pundits wondering why this would be any different than Cavs teams that have come up short in years past.

Still, Mitchell made his commitment to the Cavs because he believes in them. But he knows franchises, and especially their superstars, aren't judged by participation trophies.

"For your own mental [health], you have to embrace it and then be proud of that," he said. "In the same token, still keep the motivation of, 'You got your a- swept.'"

THE DONOVAN MITCHELL basketball camp comes to Greenwich, Connecticut, each summer.

For seven of the nine summers since Mitchell entered the NBA, Mitchell has spent a weekend hosting the event for kids from first grade through eighth, in Utah and then now in Cleveland. But he always comes back to the tristate area, where he grew up while his father worked for the New York Mets.

During his camp this offseason, Mitchell knew he was in for it. And the jokes often began with a setup that defined the Cavs' dramatic loss to the Knicks in May.

"Well, analytically ... "

It was a callback to a quote from Atkinson. At a practice before Game 4 of the conference finals, Atkinson said the Cavs were "analytically winning the series" because of expected shot metrics that showed Cleveland actually winning two of three games. Or, in other words, the Knicks were making shots they weren't supposed to make -- and the Cavaliers weren't making shots they were supposed to make.

Still, it made all the wrong headlines.

"You get swept and you look the way we looked, there's criticism and the jokes come with it," Mitchell says. "We all laugh at it, but at the same time it's like, all right, bet. Time's going to come. But hey, you got to live with it. You got to live with all parts of it."

Before a rematch with New York last week, Atkinson attempted to add context to his statement, that he was responding to a question about how the Cavs could still have belief despite trailing 3-0.

"I answered the question as it was taken," Atkinson said. "'You're down 3-0, what hope do you have of even giving your guys?' We get a lot of information, and I wasn't lying in that sense. But in no sense was it like, 'Oh man, we deserve to be winning.' Zero, zero, zero thought of that."

It's a familiar feeling for the Cavs, seeing their words become the story instead of their play.

After losing to the Knicks in the first round of the 2023 playoffs, Allen became a meme for saying "the lights were brighter than expected" after playing at Madison Square Garden.

"That's the world we live in," Cavs guard Sam Merrill told ESPN. "But we just have fun with stuff like that."

That '23 postseason was the first playoff run for Mitchell, Allen and Mobley. They advanced to the second round in the next two seasons before finally cracking the conference finals last spring.

But despite that progress, skeptics around the league point to the same throughline for the Cavs.

"All their questions will be answered in the playoffs," an Eastern Conference executive told ESPN. "But it feels like they have the same issues that have plagued them for years. Not sure what's going to be different."

ON THE MORNING of Oct. 26, Atkinson decided to put an alternative spin on the team's film session before it hosted the Minnesota Timberwolves that evening.

The Cavs had already blown a 29-point lead against the Philadelphia 76ers on opening night, becoming the first team in league history to lose the opener after building a 20-point lead at halftime.

Two nights later, the Cavs saw a 22-point fourth-quarter lead against the Brooklyn Nets get reduced to two with 8.1 seconds remaining; the Cavs held on.

Those blown leads served as a window into the doubt that has followed the team around during the Mitchell era. In Game 1 of the conference finals, the Cavs were ahead by 22 points at Madison Square Garden before collapsing in historic fashion.

Inside the film room, rather than fire up footage from one of the first few games, or even look back at the playoffs, Atkinson turned to a different sport entirely. He had his players watch clips of the England vs. Argentina match from the FIFA World Cup semi-final this past July.

England famously took a 1-0 advantage in the 55th minute, and then completely switched up their play style, falling back into a defensive formation.

Their aggression went cold; the momentum of the match shifted. Argentina rallied to a 2-1 victory to advance to the final.

"[Kenny's] just trying to find ways for it to stick in our head," Cavs forward Jaylon Tyson told ESPN. "It worked."

The Cavs put it into practice that evening. They'd trailed by 15 in the second quarter and double digits at halftime, but after 15 lead changes and five ties in the final minutes, the Cavs survived a 47-point haymaker from Anthony Edwards. Cleveland won in overtime, 127-125.

"There's a lot of belief in this group," Mitchell says. "And the way that we have been able to battle through some adversity and continue to get better and better."

Even still, Cleveland's inconsistency has continued. The Cavs lost by double digits to the Charlotte Hornets on Monday, and then bounced back to beat the Knicks in Madison Square Garden on Wednesday. No one has exemplified their up-and-down season like Harden, now in Year 18, but was brought in to be Mitchell's co-star. Harden is averaging 16.7 points and 5.6 assists while shooting 39% from the field, his lowest marks since he became a full-time starter during the 2012-13 season.

"My name is James Harden, and I used to score a lot of points," Harden said after the Cavs victory in New York. "I still score points, but I'm finding other ways to impact the game as well.

"I'm still trying to figure it out. Donovan averages a lot of points. He's a scoring machine on this team. Just picking and choosing when I have opportunities to score and then do other things to impact winning."

Despite the up-and-down start, the Cavs can look at last season as a reason for patience. They were one game over .500 on Dec. 19, before winning 52 games and securing the No.4 seed.

Mitchell sees the progress through the pain. He sees examples around the league that give him confidence in Cleveland's approach, noting how New York lost in the second round twice and in the conference finals before winning the championship.

"People tend to forget those things," he said. "That how many teams were like, 'Oh, it should be this. This guy needs to be traded. He needs to be fired.'

"All these f----ing things that happen in a lot of championship organizations right before ... "

Mitchell snapped his fingers.

"I'm not saying we're guaranteed to win, but it's just how it's been. So we can't sit here and overreact to s--- just because everybody else thinks you should."

stories.headline: Florida visits St. Louis after Lundell's 2-goal game

Florida Panthers (11-7-2, in the Atlantic Division) vs. St. Louis Blues (9-8-2, in the Central Division)


St. Louis; Saturday, 7 p.m. EST


BOTTOM LINE: The Florida Panthers visit the St. Louis Blues after Anton Lundell scored two goals in the Panthers' 5-4 win against the Detroit Red Wings.


St. Louis is 9-8-2 overall and 5-2-1 in home games. The Blues have a 7-1-1 record in games they score at least three goals.


Florida has a 6-5-2 record in road games and an 11-7-2 record overall. The Panthers lead league play with 111 total penalties (averaging 5.6 per game).

stories.headline: Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong, Astros' Yordan Alvarez unanimous MVP winners
stories.summary: Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong and the Astros' Yordan Alvarez each earned all 30 first-place votes to win the MVP awards in their respective leagues Thursday night.
stories.body:
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Houston Astros DH/OF Yordan Alvarez were named unanimous winners of the Most Valuable Player award in their respective leagues Thursday night.

Crow-Armstrong, 24, earned all 30 first-place votes for the National League MVP behind his monster season at the plate, on the bases and in the field. Four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani was second in the voting, and Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang was third.

Alvarez, 29, topped Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero and Kansas City Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. in the AL voting to capture his first MVP after a season in which he nearly won the triple crown.

New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler, the unanimous AL Cy Young winner Wednesday, placed fourth in the MVP voting. With the Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski winning the NL Cy Young unanimously, it's the first season in which both MVP winners and both Cy Young winners were unanimous.

"I'm just blessed to have the ability that I do," said Crow-Armstrong, who is the 13th player in franchise history to win the award and first since Kris Bryant in 2016. "It brings me joy to be able to affect the game a lot of times on a daily basis. ... I'm feeling lucky I was able to impact the game as much as I did this year."

A fourth-year player, Crow-Armstrong, 24, hit .280 with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases while also winning the Gold Glove and Platinum Glove awards. He also led both leagues with a 10.6 fWAR.

Crow-Armstrong began the season batting low in the lineup, often in the ninth slot. But by mid-May, he was moved to the leadoff spot and went on a tear that lasted most of the rest of the year. Cubs manager Craig Counsell said he moved Crow-Armstrong to the top of the order because the team was struggling on offense at the time and needed a spark. Crow-Armstrong took to the challenge, hitting .300 with a .398 on-base percentage while hitting first in the order. He drew 83 walks in 2026 after totaling just 29 the previous year.

Crow-Armstrong said he was thrilled that former NL MVP Andrew McCutchen made the MVP announcement on Thursday's MLB Network broadcast, calling him a player whom he "looked up to." Crow-Armstrong said he is also hopeful to inspire fans in the same way.

"I hope kids put their butts in the seats with the same sort of interest and focus that I used to," Crow-Armstrong said.

Despite winning the NL MVP, Crow-Armstrong told reporters he believed he could do better in bigger moments, such as in the postseason. He went 0-for-7 this year in the playoffs after going 5-for-27 last season.

"I'm capable but haven't gotten to the point of impacting games when it really matters," he said. "If I can take that version of myself and apply it to every aspect of the game, let's do that in October and November."

Alvarez won the AL batting title with a .316 average and finished second in home runs (42) and RBIs (106).

His unanimous MVP comes after an injury-plagued 2025 season, when he appeared in just 48 games because of a wrist fracture and a sprained ankle. He had no such bad luck this season, appearing in 158 games for the playoff-bound Astros. On Wednesday, he was also named AL Comeback Player of the Year.

"Incredible, incredible," Alvarez, speaking through an interpreter, said of his AL MVP win. "It seems like everyone else had a good feeling that I was going to win this besides me. When I heard my name, that's when the emotion came out."

Alvarez said he used his disappointing 2025 as motivation coming into this season. Asked what was different for him in 2026, Alvarez said simply, "I was healthy."

"Everyone knows what happened last year," he said. "I was anxious to get back to this season. Now, we see where that ended up, with an MVP award."

Besides winning the batting title, Alvarez drew an MLB-high 109 walks while posting a .432 on-base percentage, 46 points higher than the next-highest player.

Alvarez is the 31st player in history to win an MVP award and a rookie of the year honor. He took home the latter award in 2019 and then earned MVP votes from 2022 to 2024. He finished third in voting in 2022. He's the third Astro to win the award, joining Jeff Bagwell (1994) and Jose Altuve (2017).

stories.headline: Rapinoe, Altidore, Ertz into National Soccer Hall of Fame; Beckham gets nod
stories.summary: Former United States national team standouts Megan Rapinoe, Jozy Altidore and Julie Ertz were among those elected to the National Soccer Hall of Fame on Thursday.
stories.body:
Former United States national team standouts Megan Rapinoe, Jozy Altidore and Julie Ertz were among those elected to the National Soccer Hall of Fame on Thursday.

David Beckham, who helped grow soccer in the United States when he joined the LA Galaxy in 2007 and later as an owner of Inter Miami CF, was also voted in on the veteran ballot.

The group announced Thursday will be inducted on April 16 at the National Soccer Hall of Fame in Plano, Texas.

Rapinoe won a pair of Women's World Cup championships, an Olympic gold medal and the 2019 Ballon d'Or during her career. She was also honored with the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, in 2022.

She retired from the national team in 2023 with 63 goals and 73 assists in 203 appearances. She also played for Seattle Reign FC in the NWSL from the league's first year in 2013 until her retirement.

Rapinoe was elected on the Hall of Fame's player ballot in her first year of eligibility. Her family, friends, and a group of fans surprised her with announcement of her election upon her arrival off a flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

"To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my teammates and friends, recognized like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams. So, I definitely was a part of some some great teams, and yeah, it's very special," Rapinoe said in a video posted to social media.

Altidore played in the World Cup twice and scored 42 international goals, to rank third in U.S. history, in 115 appearances for the national team. He also scored the winning goal for Toronto FC in the 2017 MLS Cup championship.

Ertz was considered among the best defensive midfielders in the world before her retirement in 2023. She played in three Women's World Cups and was named U.S. Soccer's Player of the Year twice. She also played professionally for the NWSL's Chicago Red Stars from 2014 to 2021, before a short stint with Angel City FC in 2023.

Known for winning six Premier League titles while with Manchester United, Beckham looms large in the game's growth in the United States. He won back-to-back titles with the Galaxy, scoring 18 goals in 98 appearances. He exercised his option to buy an MLS expansion team in 2014, and Inter Miami joined the league in 2020.

"The National Soccer Hall of Fame recognizes the players and builders who have profoundly shaped the sport," MLS commissioner Don Garber said when he made the announcement to Beckham at a league board meeting. "It is my honor to welcome you to the National Soccer Hall of Fame. Congratulations David."

"This has been an incredible journey. I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this country for a long time. So thank you," Beckham said after learning of his inclusion from Garber.

Tatu, a Brazillian forward who scored 857 regular-season goals over a 21-year indoor soccer career, was also elected to the Hall of Fame on the veteran ballot. He is only the third indoor player to receive the honor.

Former U.S. national team coach Lothar Osiander was elected to the Hall of Fame on the builder ballot. Osiander coached the senior national team in 1986-88 and the Under-23 team in 1988-92. He also had stints as head coach of the then-San Jose Clash and the LA Galaxy.

stories.headline: MMA stars Merab Dvalishvili, Usman Nurmagomedov brawl at hotel in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: MMA stars Merab Dvalishvili and Usman Nurmagomedov got into a public brawl at a hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.
stories.body:
Former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov were involved in a physical altercation Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, with video of the incident widely circulated on social media.

Dvalishvili, who is in Abu Dhabi ahead of Saturday's Real American Freestyle event, posted a video of his bloodied face after the scuffle. Multiple videos of the incident showed Nurmagomedov, whose older brother, Umar, lost a bantamweight title fight to Dvalishvili in 2025, approach Dvalishvili from behind and slap him in the face.

Former UFC lightweight champion Ilia Topuria, who is friends with Dvalishvili, shared video of the encounter online. Following the initial slap, Dvalishvili attempts to go after Nurmagomedov. A chaotic scene quickly unfolded, involving multiple members from the camps of both fighters. In his video afterward, Dvalishvili refers to Nurmagomedov and his camp as "snakes."

"What a sneaky way, guys," Dvalishvili says. "What kind of fighters you guys are? What kind of man does this? If you want to try, let's do it the real way."

Abu Dhabi Police issued a statement Thursday, saying eight people were arrested for their part in the brawl, though they did not name Dvalishvili and Nurmagomedov specifically. Additionally, two people who filmed the encounter were also taken arrested. It is not clear whether any or all of the detained parties remain in custody.

UFC president Dana White, speaking at a news conference Thursday, reacted to the altercation, calling it "absolutely ridiculous and stupid."

Wednesday's confrontation marks the latest in a long-running feud between Dvalishvili and the Nurmagomedov team. Before his win over Umar in January 2025, Dvalishvili referred to Umar as "spoiled" and accused the Dagestani of being disrespectful. The two camps were involved in a brief altercation in July at another RAF event in Georgia.

Both Merab and Umar are scheduled to compete at RAF on Saturday. Dvalishvili faces former UFC title challenger Marlon Moraes, while Nurmagomedov will wrestle former UFC champion Urijah Faber.

Usman Nurmagomedov is currently in a state of restricted free agency, with much speculation whether he will leave the PFL to fight in the UFC in 2027.

stories.headline: Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad to continue at Racing Bulls for 2027
stories.summary: Liam Lawson will stay in Formula 1 alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad at Racing Bulls in 2027, ending weeks of speculation about the New Zealander's future.
stories.body:
Liam Lawson will stay in Formula 1 alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad at Racing Bulls in 2027, ending weeks of speculation about the New Zealander's future.

Lawson's place at the team had been under scrutiny in recent weeks, with Red Bull's Bulgarian junior Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings.

Racing Bulls ended any doubt on Thursday, confirming Lawson and Lindblad will continue together for another year.

Lawson has been one of the year's standout performers, sitting ninth with 89 points, a run of form which continued with a strong showing at last weekend's São Paulo Grand Prix, where he started third and finished seventh. Rookie teammate Lindblad is 11th with 38.

Racing Bulls is fighting for fifth in the constructors' championship.

- Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border, urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in'

Team boss Alan Permane, who last week signed a deal to stay in his role until 2029, said Lawson and Lindblad is the strongest lineup the team could ask for.

"We're delighted to be continuing with Liam and Arvid for 2027," Permane said. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing. I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

"Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."

Red Bull has confirmed Tsolov as reserve driver for Red Bull and Racing Bulls in 2027. The 19-year-old currently competes in Formula 2 for Campos Racing and is second in the title standings with two races remaining.

The team are promising an "extensive" programme of free practice sessions and Testing of Previous Car running as allowed under the F1 rulebook.

Tsolov said: "I'm incredibly happy and grateful to Red Bull for giving me this opportunity. Since joining the Junior Team, I've received amazing support and have developed so much, both as a driver and as a person. My career has progressed incredibly quickly, and I owe a lot to everyone who has believed in me and helped me get to this point.

"My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver. Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting. I'm confident that with the Team's support and experience, I'll have the best possible preparation to make sure I'm fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes."

stories.headline: Despite injury and illness, Gus Teixeira is still one of this year's top prospects
stories.summary: Gus Teixeira spent much of his top-age year battling injury and illness, but still found a way to be in contention to be the top pick in the open pool, writes Japser Chellappah.
stories.body:
Gustavo Teixeira had a brilliant top-age campaign. He's worked his way into pick 1 conversations, and is locked into the first handful of selections on draft night.

His success is made all the more impressive considering what's played out behind the scenes.

"I had the ankle injury at the start of the year in the first praccy game," Teixeira tells ESPN.

"It was kind of a bit annoying because every week I thought I'd be playing but it just got pushed back. I had the calf injury, I was out for five or six weeks. I rehabbed that, played a game and then the foot pulled up sore and that's why I'm not testing [at the AFL Draft combine].

"I've also been sick for basically the whole year with a virus."

Teixeira, a powerful forward-half midfielder, played valiantly through glandular fever-like symptoms that didn't get diagnosed until the conclusion of the National Championships.

He was playing games deep in the forward 50 but still finding himself short of breath and unable to hit top gear. After being diagnosed with a severe iron deficiency and receiving an infusion he felt the energy he'd been lacking return, but not before a calf injury linked to his virus took Teixeira out for all but one game in the back half of the season.

Most top-10 chances at the AFL Draft thrive off injury-free seasons where they can continually put their name up in lights. Teixeira couldn't do that this year, so he made his moments count.

His first game back from an ankle concern was in a Vic Metro trial game where he showed his worth, kicking two goals from 20 disposals in a best afield display.

"It was a good day out, I was pretty happy with that. It was annoying I couldn't do a bit more of that throughout the year but I'm sure I can do that in the future."

Teixeira had locked himself into Metro's National Championships outfit by halftime, showing off the power and class that recruiters covet.

At the National Championships he was playing under duress from his undiagnosed virus, but he still took the opportunity to show his value deep in attack.

"Obviously I was sick so I was resting a bit, I was sore the first week and they wanted me to play more forward. I kicked a few goals and they wanted me to stay down forward and that's where I was able to impact the most," he tells ESPN.

Teixeira claimed All-Australian honours, booting seven goals in his four outings including a best on ground demolition of the Allies where he kicked four goals from 22 touches.

It was an element of his game that proved his worth outside of the centre square. Teixeira got to dangerous spots and created separation with proactive running, and from there was able to demonstrate his cleanliness and class to make his chances count.

"I've always thought I want to be a midfielder, I want to play in there. Skills are very important as a midfielder so you've got to be clean and you've got to be able to kick. I'm just chipping away at it and improving."

Teixeira is of Brazilian descent via his father Matt, who was born in the city of Belo Horizonte before moving to Australia when he was 25.

He brings Gus back to Brazil every year, and that connection to a non-English speaking country would allow Teixeira to join zoned club St Kilda's Next Generation Academy if not for friction points within the AFL's own NGA rules.

"Belo Horizonte is just inland of Rio... It's like the size of Melbourne but no one's really heard of it. It's a fully different culture and it's always great to go back," he explains.

"The AFL changed the rules for the regions this year, so they allow South American people this year but you need to be in it for three years. I would've only been in it for a year... my younger siblings are in it now. I've got a brother, Eddie, who's 12 and my sister Lucy who's 14."

Like a host of the top prospects this year, Teixeira has been an Essendon supporter his whole life. The Bombers have the top pick and Teixeira is within that bracket of the pool.

"I haven't thought about the Bombers pick-wise, but just the club and thinking about what it would be like obviously going to the Bombers, it'd be great at the moment. They're getting in some good coaches and they've got some good players coming through.

"Really though I'd be stoked to get drafted to any club, moving interstate would be a pretty cool experience. I'm always trying to get the best out of myself, I've always tried to be the best at everything and just put my best foot forward so I'll do that anywhere."

stories.headline: Dirk Kuyt leaves Fenerbahce a week after defeating Liverpool
stories.summary: Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.
stories.body:
ISTANBUL -- Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.

The former Netherlands forward took charge of that 3-2 win in Istanbul despite the club already having made a deal with Emre Belözoğlu to take over.

Kuyt returned in July to Fenerbahce, where he played from 2012-15, to assist coach Ismail Kartal who resigned last month.

"We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for all that you have contributed to these colors," Fenerbahce said in a social media post announcing Kuyt's exit. "Today we say goodbye to you but your place in this big family will never change."

Belözoğlu, a former captain of the club, takes over a team sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the 36-team Champions League standings.

Fenerbahce's next Champions League opponent is Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Wings' Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd talk relationship on pod
stories.summary: Azzi Fudd hosted Wings teammate Paige Bueckers on her podcast and the two discussed their relationship, Dallas' season and Fudd's recovery from knee surgery.
stories.body:
Dallas Wings teammates Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers, the past two WNBA No. 1 draft picks, spoke on Fudd's podcast Friday about a variety of topics, including a personal life update.

"We're not together anymore; it's been a while," Bueckers said on the "Fudd Around and Find Out" podcast. "[We] share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Bueckers and Fudd, who were teammates in college at UConn, said they felt the need to address their relationship status in part because of allegations it factored into the Wings picking Fudd at No. 1 in April. Fudd was chosen over TCU guard Olivia Miles, who went on to be the Rookie of the Year for the Minnesota Lynx. Spain's Awa Fam (Seattle Storm) was taken third, followed by teammates from the 2026 champion UCLA Bruins: Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics), Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) and Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo).

Fudd, Fam, Betts and Miles were all No. 1 at different points in ESPN's mock draft in the months before the April draft. Bueckers said her previous relationship with Fudd had no impact on Dallas' decision.

"We were not together before she got drafted," Bueckers said. "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points but was limited to just 30 games after an injury to her right knee led to season-ending arthroscopic surgery in August. She offered an update on her health.

"My offseason's been good," Fudd said. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy.

"I think there's a lot I can improve on. Especially the iso game; I feel like I'm not too comfortable with that yet. I know I'm capable of doing a little bit more. Watching someone like Paige who is able to create from anywhere ... that's great inspiration for me."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists, and was named to the All-WNBA second team as Dallas reached the playoffs as the No. 7 seed.

The Wings were eliminated in the first round by the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries. Bueckers said she learned a lot from her first playoff experience and complimented Golden State.

"The Valkyries' defense, I can't explain to you how tough they are," Bueckers said. "They swarm, they send bodies, they trap you, they blitz you, they're so connected. I'm glad I got to have that experience against them to open my eyes to what the playoffs are like -- the physicality, the pressure, the environment.

"And I'm proud of our season. I hated losing; I sat and was pissed about it for like a week. I reached out to [Sue Bird] about it, what was her first playoff experience like. I didn't play as well as I wanted to. But it was my first experience, going against a really good opponent, and I was learning and growing through it all."

Fudd and Bueckers also addressed the Wings' move to the 19,000-seat American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas next season after playing at UT Arlington's College Park Center, which seats over 7,000, since the franchise relocated to Texas in 2016.

"UTA was a vibe; we had a ball, we did our thing there," Bueckers said. "But definitely excited to move into Dallas. New times."

While the change in venue will lead to more eyes on Wings games, the two players said they're hoping for less scrutiny of any on-court behavior.

Both said fans shouldn't read into interactions the two have with each other or their teammates as anything other than normal team behavior. They also said they don't stand for "hate of any kind" or "tearing people down to lift us up."

"We've seen a lot of negativity," Bueckers said. "We've had stuff sent to us, stuff sent to our family, our friends. There's been some crazy things said about us. We still support each other, we're still going to be great friends, we're still going to be great teammates. All the negative things can be put aside, and you don't need to overanalyze everything."

Fudd added with a chuckle, "Also, we don't need messages [from fans] on what the other person's doing. We've addressed everything we need to, and the rest will stay with us."

stories.headline: Why Kiwi sharp-shooter is taking Cup final personally
stories.summary: Jamayne Isaako is on a remarkable personal run entering the World Cup final, where he has a score to settle with an NRL teammate.
stories.body:
Jamayne Isaako is taking it personally as a generational New Zealand team attempts to break Australia's World Cup stranglehold in their Brisbane decider.

The Kiwis will face the Kangaroos at Suncorp Stadium on Sunday, attempting to win a second cup and first since 2008.

The hosts have won nine of the last 10 tournaments but will be challenged by a side that did everything but win in a 24-22 loss to begin the tournament.

Australian winger Jack Bostock scored a hat trick on debut, twice leaping above Dolphins teammate Isaako for tries while also plucking an intercept.

Isaako, who will leave for the Melbourne Storm next season after 11 campaigns with Brisbane's, Gold Coast's and Redcliffe's NRL clubs, hasn't forgotten.

"Not to take him lightly," Isaako said of what he took from that duel.

"It wasn't something I incorporated into my prep; his height and reach there.

"So it's something I'll be taking personally this weekend, hopefully I can stop him and do a better job."

Bostock played in the centres - on the same side of the field as Isaako - in the New Zealander's last season at the Dolphins and the pair were able to laugh about the contest when they reunited for a photo-shoot this week.

"He gave me a little bit of stick," Isaako said.

The 30-year-old maintains belief is high, pointing to the side's 2023 Pacific Champions triumph as a turning point for the team and himself. The goal-kicker was left out of the Kiwis side for four years before his 2023 return and has played 13 consecutive Test and 98 consecutive NRL games since.

"There's a lot of confidence about what we've been able to create here," he said.

"I don't think we're ever going to get a squad (this good) again, so it's about making the most of the moments we get together.

"I'm certainly going to miss this place (living in Brisbane) and I'd like to finish on a high, hopefully holding the World Cup."

stories.headline: What to know to set your lineup: Cousins' Vikings return elevates Jefferson
stories.summary: Adam Rank catches you up on the vital information and insight before you make your toughest lineup decisions.
stories.body:
Have you ever been in a relationship that was so bad, you yearned for the one who got away? Because if you did, you might just be the Minnesota Vikings. And that bad relationship might be with Carson Wentz. Just kidding. It was with Wentz. And the rift was very public, too, happening on "Monday Night Football."

I'm not saying Wentz was bad, but it was hard to watch. Like a couple breaking up in the middle of a mall. You don't want to look, but at the same time, you want to walk to Auntie Anne's, grab a pretzel and enjoy the show.

The Vikings then moved on very quickly. I'm talking about the time it took Kathy to move on with her co-star after her big fight with Chandler. (Yes, I tend to have "Friends" reruns on in the background here while the kids are asleep.)

The Vikings turned to Kirk Cousins rather quickly. The veteran quarterback said it was good to be back because Kevin O'Connell knew him so well. Yeah, well enough to let you walk years ago, draft J.J. McCarthy, sign Sam Darnold and Daniel Jones. Let Sam Darnold walk to Seattle, where he'd win a Super Bowl. Let Jones walk to Indianapolis. Trade McCarthy to the Giants. Sign Carson Wentz. Sign Kyler Murray. And then trade for you. Yes, he knows you so well.

But the good news is Cousins is back in Minnesota. And I tend to look at this reunion the same way I look at a reunion between Jon Favreau and Vince Vaughn. They hit it out of the park with "Swingers," but "Made" might have been one of the worst movies ever made, pun intended. Still, having Cousins back is great for Justin Jefferson, who seemingly has been shooting daggers at all involved for his downfall. T.J. Hockenson has been great and he gets a big boost.

Shifting gears, you should check out my Bye-mageddon column published Wednesday to get you prepared for next week, when six teams are sitting out. But now, let's look at what you need to know in Week 10.

Quarterbacks

Puka Nacua isn't on IR, but he won't play. Davante Adams is still out. So it's really tough to trust Matthew Stafford despite the fact the Arizona Cardinals have allowed 20.9 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Stafford has averaged just 12.3 fantasy points per game from Weeks 7-9.
Trevor Lawrence is a must-start this week, as he's averaged 18-plus over his past three games. The Tennessee Titans are top 10 in fantasy points allowed to the position. There's always a risk because the Jaguars can dominate and dial it back. But I'm undaunted.
Jordan Love has perhaps the toughest of matchups this week. I'd still take him over the streaming options like Drew Lock, Geno Smith and Aaron Rodgers.

Running backs

Braelon Allen is still getting 73% of the snaps, but Breece Hall received more carries. A lot of his production was in garbage time last week. But he's still a good flex option this week against the Buffalo Bills.
Kyren Williams and Blake Corum are both starts for me this week. Corum has fewer than 40% of the snaps, but has scored a touchdown in five consecutive games. Not always sustainable, but I have to believe the Los Angeles Rams' game plan has to include him as the runner, with Williams moving into more of a receiver role.
Disappointment reigns for Chase Brown, but he's still up around 70% of the snaps. The Pittsburgh Steelers aren't a great matchup, but I still play the volume here.
Kaelon Black is seeing his usage increase each week for the San Francisco 49ers. This is an older team that got older at the trade deadline. The Dallas Cowboys are fourth in fantasy points allowed to running backs. He's getting early-down work. Black is a comfortable flex option.

Wide receiver

KC Concepcion has averaged 16.2 over the past three weeks, up from 7.9 before that. The Houston Texans aren't a great matchup, but he's playing 85% of the snaps.
Jakobi Meyers is a fun flex play against the Tennessee Titans, who have allowed the most fantasy points to receivers this year. One of my top requirements when looking for flex receivers is who is the quarterback. Lawrence is one of the best.
I don't know how you bench Drake London. And I'm not saying to do it. But the Chiefs have allowed the second-fewest points to receivers this season.

Tight ends

Not only is Hunter Henry a great start this week, as the Detroit Lions have allowed 25.1 fantasy points per game to tight ends, but they allow a lot of touchdowns to the position. And if you need a flier, Eli Raridon has played on nearly 70% of the snaps for New England.
Tyler Warren isn't quite in bust territory for the Indianapolis Colts, but I expect an uptick in production with Keenan Allen and Josh Downs traded to playoff contenders.
I can't believe I'm going to say this -- yes, I can -- but Tucker Kraft is a tough start. The Vikings are brutal to opposing tight ends, allowing the fewest points to the position. Need a streaming defense? Baltimore Ravens. They were once the go-to defense in fantasy football. Now they are a team that you stream.

stories.headline: Mauricio Pochettino agrees Man United deal, announcement expected - sources
stories.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the next Manchester United manager with an announcement expected on Friday, sources have told ESPN.
stories.body:
Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the next Manchester United manager with an announcement expected on Friday, sources have told ESPN.

The 54-year-old will replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked by the club on Thursday. Pochettino has finalised personal terms on a two-and-a-half year contract at Old Trafford.

He has agreed a deal with the U.S. Soccer which will see him take charge of two games against Haiti, on Nov. 14 and Nov. 17, before traveling to Manchester.

United expect Pochettino at Carrington on Wednesday ahead of his first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22. The bulk of United's international players will also return to Carrington on Wednesday.

Sources have told ESPN that United CEO Omar Berrada told U.S. Soccer on Wednesday that they would trigger the $10 million (£7.5m) release clause in Pochettino's contract. United are expected to pay another $2m to hire Pochettino's staff, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez.

Pochettino, according to sources, asked representatives to alert United to the existence of a release clause in the contract extension he signed with U.S. Soccer in August.

stories.headline: Who has won the MLB MVP Award? All-time winners list
stories.summary: MLB's MVP Award is given to top players in the American League and National League. Take a look at the all-time winners list now.
stories.body:
There are two MVPs in Major League Baseball each year -- one in the American League and one in the National League. Since 1931, the Baseball Writers' Association of America has voted for the MVPs at the end of the regular season and before the start of the postseason.

The award began in 1911 as the Chalmers Award, honoring the "most important and useful player to the club and to the league." That award was discontinued in 1914. From 1922 to 1928 in the AL and from 1924 to 1929 in the NL, the League Award was presented to "the baseball player who is of the greatest all-around service to his club." Prior winners were not eligible to win the award again during that time.

In 2026, Yordan Alvarez of the Houston Astros won MVP for the American League, the 3rd Astros player to win the award after Jose Altuve in 2017 and Jeff Bagwell in 1994. Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs won for the National League, the first Cubs player to win it since Kris Bryant in 2016.

stories.headline: Messi up for record 3rd MLS MVP award; Sullivan, 17, gets historic nomination
stories.summary: Lionel Messi has been named a finalist for the 2026 MLS MVP award, as he seeks to become the first player to win the prize on three consecutive occasions.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi has been named a finalist for the 2026 Major League Soccer MVP award, as the Inter Miami captain seeks to become the first player to win the prize on three consecutive occasions.

Messi won the MVP award in 2024 and 2025, becoming the second player to ever win the trophy twice, alongside Preki (Predrag Radosavljević), who won the title in 1997 and 2003.

- Will MLS teams' regular-season momentum last the two weeks before the playoffs start?

- Every eliminated MLS team: What worked and what didn't in 2026, what needs improving in 2027?

- Brotherly love: Cavan, Quinn Sullivan both score as Philly soars into playoffs

Eight-time Ballon d'Or winner Messi already clinched a record second straight Golden Boot award after scoring 26 goals in the 2026 regular season.

Messi joins finalists Evander (FC Cincinnati), Guilherme (Houston Dynamo FC) Hany Mukhtar (Nashville SC), and Cavan Sullivan (Philadelphia Union) for the award, which is named after former U.S. men's national team great Landon Donovan.

At 17 years old, Sullivan stands as the youngest player in MLS history to be named a finalist for the MVP award. He is also a finalist for the MLS Young Player of the Year award.

Last month, Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history when he found the net against Mexico.

MVP candidate Guilherme was named a finalist for the MLS Newcomer of the Year award, alongside Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City SC). Guilherme recorded 16 goals and 10 assists, while Griezmann managed 14 goals and eight assists.

Griezmann earns the recognition after joining Orlando City in July after finishing the 2025-26 season with Atlético Madrid in Spain.

Finalists for each end-of-the-year award received the highest average in votes from MLS club technical staff, MLS first-team players and select media members. Each group accounted for 33.3% of the overall results, according to MLS.

Winners will be announced during the 2026 playoffs, which begin on Nov. 19.

stories.headline: UFC's Josh Hokit says he'll 'never' regret vulgar Michelle Obama remarks
stories.summary: UFC fighter Josh Hokit, who will challenger for the heavyweight title on Saturday, says he'll "never" regret his vulgar comments about former First Lady Michelle Obama,
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- UFC heavyweight Josh Hokit said he has no regrets about using the White House as a bully pulpit to make an extraordinary and unfounded attack based on a right-wing conspiracy theory about former first lady Michelle Obama.

Hokit made his vulgar remarks inside the Octagon in June after winning his fight at the UFC event to mark President Donald Trump's 80th birthday on the South Lawn of the White House.

Hokit fights for the first time since then on Saturday when he challenges heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden.

Hokit again made a series of crass insults about other fighters on the fight card on Wednesday inside a New York hotel before taking questions about his championship bout and his remarks on Obama.

"I'll never look back and be like, I regret that," Hokit said.

Wearing a black stocking cap over an American flag bandana, sunglasses and fight gloves, Hokit said he "took the rap of a villain" before he burst into what he called a freestyle rap to express his lack of regret.

Hokit said he was "sure it wasn't" the right thing to do to insult the former first lady but was proud the remarks had put his image on Trump's Truth Social posts. In one post, Hokit appeared in cartoon form alongside UFC chief Dana White in the White House briefing room.

Trump said over the weekend he had offered White the job of White House press secretary. White declined the frivolous offer.

"I'm here to take what's mine," Hokit said. "If I've got to rub some people the wrong way, if I've got to say some (stuff) in the wrong location, it is what it is. Was it not a good location to say it? I mean, we're at the White House. That house represents freedom of speech. So it is what it is. I think it was the perfect location to say it."

The 28-year-old Hokit is 10-0 in his MMA career and has won all six fights since joining UFC in 2025.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border, urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to let aid trucks into Gaza after visiting the Rafah border this week, adding in a passionate post "the past three years of Israel's genocide is appalling."
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to let aid trucks into Gaza after visiting the Rafah border this week, adding in a passionate post "the past three years of Israel's genocide is appalling."

The seven-time world champion called for a "Free Palestine" during a news conference ahead of October's United States Grand Prix, and has previously called for a ceasefire in the region.

This week, Hamilton visited the Rafah crossing, the only land crossing between the Gaza Strip and Egypt and the hub of various humanitarian aid organizations.

After meeting aid workers and truck drivers on the ground, Hamilton posted a message about the trip to his 44 million Instagram followers.

"The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling," Hamilton wrote on Instagram. "It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less."

Israel denies accusations of genocide, saying its military campaign in Gaza targets militants of terrorist group Hamas. Hamilton urged people not to ignore what is happening in the region.

"I know so many people that feel that same helplessness," he added. "That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away."

- Qatar, Abu Dhabi races set to go ahead as F1 rules out Imola backup plan for finale

Hamilton also met with North Sinai Governor Khaled Megawer.

The governor's office shared videos to its official Facebook page of Hamilton being briefed by Megawer on the aid coordination and the Ferrari driver greeting aid workers and inquiring how often they were able to enter Gaza through the Rafah crossing.

Last month, the World Health Organization (WHO) said repeated delays in bringing life-saving medicines, prosthetics and other supplies into Gaza can have "devastating consequences" for Palestinians who urgently need them.

Hamilton described seeing food trucks lined up and ready to go in, only to be delayed or not allowed in.

His post continued: "I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help.

"At the Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they're regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours. At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids.

"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse."

Essendon will be on the clock first, holding the top selection a decade on from the last time it took the number one pick to the AFL Draft. The Dons are expected to first bid on Port Adelaide-tied forward Dougie Cochrane, which will trigger a start-of-second-round compensation pick for the Bombers, Tigers and Eagles.

There are familial lines drawn throughout an exciting 2008-born cohort. Cody Walker is the son of high-flying Blue Andrew and will be headed to Princes Park. Cochrane is the son of former North Melbourne and Port Adelaide midfielder Stuart, though he isn't eligible to either team under the 100-game father-son rule. Instead, he's eligible to join the Power as part of their Next Generation Academy as an Indigenous prospect.

Top-10 riser Sam Gayfer is the nephew of 1990 premiership Pie Mick, and Koby LeCras brings goalkicking pedigree via 2018 premiership uncle Mark.

There will be up to five club-tied talents picked in the first round of the AFL Draft. But that won't necessarily result in an extended first night. Over the past five years the first round has averaged out to 25 selections accounting for father-son and academy bids, but clubs are expecting a number closer to the traditional 18 picks in the final intake of the 18-team competition.

Stricter stipulations around matching bids is at play, with clubs only able to use a maximum of two selections when matching for a club-tied prospect, meaning the selections of Port Adelaide, Carlton, Brisbane and GWS will be absorbed as early bids are matched.

We could see a record number of Indigenous talents picked in the first round. The high-water mark was four in 2005 and 2014, and all of Cochrane, Walker, Caylen Murray (Lions Academy), Toby Krasna and Jake Eime could be taken in the first round in 2026.

Thirteen of the top prospects have already been invited to Marvel Stadium on November 19.

Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody are all still in contention to be the open pool No. 1 pick, with Harry Van Hattum, Gus Teixeira, Mitch Harris and Ethan Matthews (Giants Academy) rounding out the group on top of draft boards alongside Cochrane and Walker.

Murray, Gayfer, Wil Malady and Leo Steed have also received invites in a sign of club interest on night one.

Around 65 picks are expected to be taken across both nights which would surpass the 60 selections last year.
